text:
alisa: Heads up — hitting a weird accuracy + perf regression when serving AWQ-int8 through TensorRT-LLM on A100s. Repro steps and logs below. Anyone seen cuBLASLt / kernel fallback issues with mixed AWQ/GPTQ artifacts? @cheng @dino

alisa: Quick numbers from MMLU eval (same prompt set): FP16 baseline: 71.2%
AWQ-int8 (served via TRT-LLM image): 68.4%
GPTQ (served via native vLLM): 70.9%
Latency (p99 single-request): FP16: ~90ms, AWQ+TRT-LLM: ~130ms. GPU util looks lower during AWQ runs.

dino: Can you paste image / driver / CUDA versions you used?

alisa: Image: nvcr.io/redwood/tensorrt-llm:2.1.0-awq + awq-runtime v0.7 (pip). Host driver: 535.86.05, CUDA toolkit inside image: 12.3. Model: llama-2-13b quantized with AWQ (mixed 4/8 config) using awq-quantize v0.7.

maria: Lower accuracy + higher latency usually indicates a kernel fallback to a slow path or host memcpy. Any "CUBLAS_STATUS" or "no kernel found" errors in the logs?

alisa: Snip of the error stream:
```
[W tensorrt_llm] cublasLt error: CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED while selecting int8 matmul kernel
[W awq_kernels] falling back to reference int8 GEMM (very slow)
[INFO] using fallback GEMM path for layer 42
```

maria: That matches what I've seen when TensorRT-LLM picks a kernel requiring a newer cuBLASLt API or when the awq custom kernels were built against a different CUDA ABI. Two checks: (1) is the awq native extension built inside the container against CUDA 12.3? (2) does the TRT-LLM image vendor a cuBLASLt that conflicts with host driver?

cheng: Quick debugging checklist we've used:
- Try TRT-LLM 2.0.2 image (we had 2.1.0 introduce a cuBLASLt selector change).
- Try host driver downgrade to 525.x (CUDA 12.2 compatible driver) as a cross-check.
- Rebuild awq native ops wheel inside the target image (pip wheel built against same CUDA).
- Run NVTX traces or `nsys` to see if kernels are dispatched to device or falling back.

sam-k: Additional note: AWQ's int8 kernels use custom CUDA kernels that must be compiled with the exact same major.minor CUDA version to avoid ABI mismatches. If you installed a prebuilt wheel on top of the NVIDIA image, it might still be compiled for a different cudart/cuBLASLt. Rebuild: `pip install --no-binary :all: awq-ops` inside the TRT image.

alisa: Reproduction command I used (simplified):
```
docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v /models:/models \
  nvcr.io/redwood/tensorrt-llm:2.1.0-awq \
  bash -c "python bench.py --model /models/llama2-13b-awq --quant awq --backend trt_llm --eval mmlu --bs 1"
```

dino: Can you also dump `ldd` of the awq extension lib and `pip show awq-ops`? That will show which libcublas / libcublasLt SONAME was linked.

alisa: Yep, ldd shows `libcublasLt.so.12 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12` (provided by container). `pip show awq-ops` shows wheel compiled for cuda110 or cuda116 (mismatch!).

maria: Bingo. Mismatch in the wheel. Two practical paths: (A) rebuild awq-ops wheel inside this image (fast), or (B) use TRT-LLM image that vendors a matching cuBLASLt and awq wheel. Option A is our typical dev path.

cheng: If you want a quick check that it's not TRT-LLM logic, try serving the same AWQ quant file with vLLM native runtime (no TensorRT). If vLLM shows correct accuracy near 71 and expected latency profile, then it's likely a TRT/awq kernel mismatch rather than quantization quality issue.

alisa: I ran that earlier: AWQ file served with vLLM native gave 69.8 (still a small drop vs GPTQ), but importantly it did not show the cublasLt fallback warnings and latency was ~110ms. So AWQ quant quality delta ~1.4-2.8 points vs GPTQ depending on serving path; the big drop to 68.4 was only with TRT-LLM image and the fallback logs.

sam-k: Also check the quant post-processing glue — some TRT-LLM integrations convert int8 blocks into different alignment that can change rounding behavior. We had a case where packing into int8x4 changed exponent alignment and shifted logits slightly. Small numeric changes can push some answers over/under thresholds in MMLU.

maria: Good to capture as a triage run:
1) Rebuild awq-ops inside TRT image and re-run (expected to remove fallback and fix perf)
2) Run test with TRT-LLM 2.0.2 image + current wheel (control)
3) Run with host driver 525.x + 12.2 toolchain (if (1)/(2) fail)
Track: accuracy, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU SM util, and nvprof traces for a failing layer.

alisa: Plan accepted. I'll run (1)-(3) overnight and post numbers tomorrow morning. Will also attach the `ldd` and `pip show` outputs and full nvprof trace. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Job queued: infra/ci-rebuild-awq-wheel (id: 98432). You will be notified when it finishes.

alisa: Great — adding this to the QA checklist for onboarding new quant models: ensure quant ops wheel is built inside target serving image and add a short kernel-sanity smoke test that fails the build if fallback paths are used.

maria: Also file a short runbook note in the eng-ml wiki so SREs know which combos are supported (CUDA/driver/TRT-LLM/awq-ops) to avoid surprise regressions in Dedicated/Private installs.

cheng: FYI I'll open a follow-up GH issue on TRT-LLM repo referencing our logs so we can get vendor guidance if 2.0.2 vs 2.1.0 behavior differs.

alisa: Thanks everyone — will report back with numbers.
